deep.reconstruction:
This page has no mathematical derivations. It continues a series of aphorisms and reflections from Hilbert's notebook (Cod. Ms. Hilbert 600:3).

(1) The page opens by finishing a remark begun on the previous folio. It cites Helmholtz, 'Vorträge und Reden', p. 51, and says that something is no longer done today, 'although the execution can be very difficult'. The context is lost on the preceding leaf.

(2) Proving consistency ('Widerspruchslosigkeit') is always a main task. The reason given: from the slightest, however hidden, contradiction any absurdity whatever can be derived. In modern terms this is ex contradictione quodlibet: (A and not A) implies B, for every B. It is illustrated with a Latin example sentence: 'Bructerus mons superat omnes Hercyniae montes', i.e. 'the Brocken surpasses all the Harz mountains'.

(3) A quotation 'from a postcard to Frege'. Its gist is Hilbert's implicit-definition view of axioms:
- A concept can be fixed logically only by its relations to other concepts.
- These relations, formulated in definite statements, are the axioms.
- Hence the axioms (possibly together with the name-giving conventions) are the definitions of the concepts.
- He says he did not devise this view 'for amusement'. He was forced to it by the demand for rigour in logical inference and in the logical construction of a theory.
- In mathematics and the natural sciences, subtler matters can only be treated rigorously this way; otherwise one merely goes in circles.

(4) An aphorism parodying Schiller (Braut von Messina: 'Die Welt ist vollkommen überall, wo der Mensch nicht hinkommt mit seiner Qual'): 'Mathematics is perfect everywhere the index-pusher (?) does not reach with his torment.' This is a jab at mechanical index or formula calculation, consistent with the next page's contrast between the old reign of the calculus and the coming 'operating with concepts'.

(5) 'Arithmetic provides the best entrance gates to mathematics, geometry the best means of communication', continued onto the next page.

The only logical content is in (2) and (3). Nothing needs to be computed.
errors: No mathematical errors, since there are no computations.

The Latin illustration of a 'Verkehrtheit' (absurdity) is odd as an example. The Brocken (Mons Bructerus) really is the highest summit of the Harz (Hercynia/Hercynian forest), so the sentence as transcribed is true rather than absurd. Either the reading is wrong, or the intended absurd sentence differs, or Hilbert meant something else by the example. This needs checking against the image.

The Frege quotation on the page is a slightly condensed or paraphrased version of what appears in the published correspondence. The parenthetical about name-giving definitions and the word 'Strenge' versus 'Sicherheit' should be compared with the printed text (Frege, Wissenschaftlicher Briefwechsel). I am not certain which Hilbert letter or postcard the printed text comes from (the Dec. 1899 letter vs. a later postcard).

results.what: From any contradiction every proposition follows, so consistency proofs are a principal task of axiomatics.
results.modern_name: Ex falso (contradictione) quodlibet / principle of explosion; consistency as the central metamathematical requirement
results.usually_credited_to: Medieval logic (Pseudo-Scotus); as a programmatic demand for consistency proofs, Hilbert himself (Grundlagen der Geometrie 1899, Paris problem 2, 1900)

results.what: Axioms as implicit definitions of the primitive concepts, as stated in the correspondence with Frege.
results.usually_credited_to: David Hilbert (Frege–Hilbert correspondence 1899–1903); also Gergonne earlier

results.what: Methodological aphorisms: mathematics perfect where index-calculators don't reach; arithmetic as entrance, geometry as means of communication.
results.usually_credited_to: Hilbert (notebook aphorisms, partly quoted in literature by Corry, Rowe, Sieg, Hallett)

deep.surprise_reason: The page contains well-known Hilbert positions: consistency as the main task, and axioms as implicit definitions. The Frege quotation is from his published correspondence with Frege. The aphorisms are characteristic but not mathematically substantive.

transcription_corrections: 'Bructerus[?] mons superat omnes Hercyniae montes': the hand seems to show a form like 'Bructerus' (possibly misspelled), underlined. The reading is plausible but uncertain.
'Indexixer[?]' is unclear. Given the Schiller parody, Hilbert probably means an index-calculator or index-pusher (perhaps 'Indexrechner' or 'Indicesmensch'); needs palaeographic check.

The insertion 'ev. nach den Namengebungen' is written above the line between 'Axiome' and 'die Definitionen'. Likewise 'und beim logischen Aufbau einer Theorie' is an interlinear insertion after 'Strenge beim logischen Schliessen'. Both are correctly placed in the transcription.
